title: Emergent abilities, drawn honestly
prompt: An optional God node was found in an interna-communication graph. It suggested there's a hard-to-find latent structure somewhere inside between 2 sub-graphs. Walk it.

compose.title: Emergent abilities, drawn honestly
compose.shows: One example's capability curve with both aggregates drawn over it. The thresholded aggregate shadows the continuous one exactly when the examples' thresholds coincide — you can watch it happen. The sweep runs on the same page, same code.

table.caption: One threshold-coincidence sweep, watched while it runs: the page re-runs this sweep in the browser, live, on the same code as the curves. A cell surpassed is the thresholded aggregate's 10→90 width; a red cell means it shadows the continuous width by 40% or more.

items.text: Pre-registered observable: 10→90 width of each aggregate curve, computed from the same 200 latent curves. Fixed before the sweep ran.
The sweep in the page is not a replay: it re-executes the sim core in your browser and fills the table as it goes. Live cells and this pinned table are two runs of one code path.

The mirage has a name: when thresholds coincide (sigma <= 0.15) the thresholded aggregate jumps inside 0.013-0.063 of x while the continuous curve needs 0.037-0.375. Same examples, same capabilities, two stories.
The mirage disappears when thresholds spread (sigma = 0.5-1.5): both aggregates widen together (0.212-0.733). Accuracy jumps measure luck in threshold placement, not the size of the leap.

What the sim leaves out: real capability curves are not logistic shifts — real benchmarks carry confounding, and training itself creates the thresholds. This prices the artifact; it does not settle whether any given claimed emergence is one.
One sim core drives the curves, the in-page sweep, and this table (sha256 pinned in Experiment#1660's config).
